英文原标题：Town Raises $108 Million at $1 Billion Valuation for Team AI Assistants（中文为 AI 翻译，仅供参考）

Imagine AI helpers that don't just manage your inbox but chat with your teammates' assistants to keep projects moving without the wait.

Town, an AI startup, secured $108 million in Series B funding, co-led by Forerunner Ventures and Menlo Ventures, pushing its valuation to $1 billion. The company launched its public product in June, hitting seven figures in annual recurring revenue with paying customers growing fourfold since July. Townies connect to workplace tools, learn individual styles, and now coordinate directly with each other for smoother team handoffs—addressing CEO Jean-Denis Greze's point that work's biggest bottleneck is waiting on others. Investors like Menlo Ventures, which uses it firm-wide, praise the focus on real tasks and rapid adoption across thousands of businesses.

Jean-Denis Greze was CTO of Plaid. His next startup, an AI tax product for small businesses, brought in nearly $1M in revenue its first year, and he projected $2.5 to $3M the next. He shut it down anyway.

The reason: in the age of AI, it was never going to be venture scale. Incumbents could use the same technology to automate tax prep for their existing customers faster than a startup could win market share. Tax is also sold once a year, so he had about a one-month window to pivot before the door closed.

The pivot became Town, an AI assistant that works from your email and calendar. It found product-market fit fast enough that Ben Horowitz messaged a16z's Alex Rampell to say it "changed my life."

In this conversation, Alex and Jean-Denis cover:

- How to know when to kill a business that's working on paper

- Why Town competes with OpenAI and Anthropic, the companies it buys its tokens from

- Why the "forward deployed engineer" model gets worse as AI gets better

- How a $1/month AI routine can save a restaurant thousands

- What agents mean for Amazon, advertising and the future of shopping
